'''Walter Greiner''' (29 October 1935 – 6 October 2016) was a German [[theoretical physicist]] and professor of the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]]. His research interests lay in [[atomic physics]], [[heavy ion physics]], [[nuclear physics]], elementary [[particle physics]] (particularly in [[quantum electrodynamics]] and [[quantum chromodynamics]]). He is known for his series of books in theoretical physics, particularly in Germany but also around the world.

==Biography==

Walter Greiner was born on 29 October 1935, in [[Neuenbau]], [[Sonneberg (district)|district of Sonneberg]], Germany.<ref>{{Citation|last=Faessler|first=Amand|chapter=In Memoriam Walter Greiner 1935–2016. Was Bleibt?: FIAS International Symposion on Discoveries of Science. Summary Talk|date=2020|chapter-url=http://link.Springer.com/10.1007/978-3-030-34234-0_23|title=Discoveries at the Frontiers of Science|series=FIAS Interdisciplinary Science Series |pages=351–374|editor-last=Kirsch|editor-first=Johannes|publisher=Springer International Publishing|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-34234-0_23|isbn=978-3-030-34233-3|s2cid=216191254 |access-date=7 May 2020|editor2-last=Schramm|editor2-first=Stefan|editor3-last=Steinheimer-Froschauer|editor3-first=Jan|editor4-last=Stöcker|editor4-first=Horst|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He studied physics at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]] receiving a BSci in physics, a master's degree in 1960 with a thesis on plasma reactors working with [[Otto Scherzer]].<ref name=":0" /> Greiner obtained his PhD in 1961 at the [[University of Freiburg]] under {{ill|Hans Marschall|de|Hans Marschall (Physiker)}}, with a thesis titled ''Nuclear polarization in muonic atoms'' ({{Langx|de|Die Kernpolarisation in μ-Mesoatomen}}).<ref name=":0">{{Citation |last=Mişicu |first=Şerban |chapter=The Early Work of Walter Greiner (1960–1968) |date=2018 |title=Walter Greiner Memorial Volume |pages=9–22 |chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789813234284_0002 |access-date=31 October 2024 |publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC |language=en |doi=10.1142/9789813234284_0002 |isbn=978-981-323-427-7|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> From 1962 to 1964, he was assistant professor at the [[University of Maryland]], followed by a Research Associate position at the [[University of Freiburg]] in 1964.<ref>[http://bitp.kiev.ua/en/doctors/greiner Bogolyubov institute for Theoretical Physics]</ref>

Starting in 1965, he became a full professor at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at Goethe University Frankfurt until 1995.

Greiner has been a visiting professor to many universities and laboratories, including [[Florida State University]], the [[University of Virginia]], the [[University of California]], the [[University of Melbourne]], [[Vanderbilt University]], [[Yale University]], [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]], and [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].

In 2003, with [[Wolf Singer]], he was the founding Director of the [[Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies]] (FIAS), and gave lectures and seminars in elementary particle physics. He died on 6 October 2016 at the age of 80.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.trauer-rheinmain.de/traueranzeige/walter-greiner/48255029 |title=Traueranzeige |access-date=20 October 2016 |archive-date=25 October 2016 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20161025010353/https://www.trauer-rheinmain.de/traueranzeige/walter-greiner/48255029 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After Greiner's death, several books and articles were published as tributes to him.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://link.Springer.com/10.1007/978-3-030-34234-0|title=Discoveries at the Frontiers of ==Graduate students==

His doctoral students include [[Berndt Müller]], [[Johann Rafelski]]<ref>{{Citation|last=Rafelski|first=Johann|chapter=Die Erste Stunde (The First Hour)|date=2020|chapter-url=http://link.Springer.com/10.1007/978-3-030-34234-0_22|title=Discoveries at the Frontiers of Science|series=FIAS Interdisciplinary Science Series|pages=331–349|editor-last=Kirsch|editor-first=Johannes|publisher=Springer International Publishing|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-34234-0_22|isbn=978-3-030-34233-3|access-date=7 May 2020|editor2-last=Schramm|editor2-first=Stefan|editor3-last=Steinheimer-Froschauer|editor3-first=Jan|editor4-last=Stöcker|editor4-first=Horst|arxiv=1804.09909|s2cid=119335943}}</ref> and [[Horst Stöcker]].

==Awards==

Greiner has received numerous scientific awards, including the [[Max Born Prize]] in 1974, the [[Otto Hahn Prize]] in 1982, and the [[Alexander von Humboldt Medal]].<ref>[https://physics.aps.org/authors/walter_greiner American Physical Society]</ref> Many of his students are holders of chairs at home and abroad or employees at renowned scientific institutions.

==Books==

Greiner's books cover most of theoretical physics, although there are more in the areas of his research (quantum mechanics and field theory, with applications). The following are the English translations of the books. See the [[:de:Walter Greiner|German Wikipedia]] for the original German editions (which include a volume on [[hydrodynamics]], not published in the English series).
